title: Checkpoint: Layout Clinic Verdict
prompt: ISO C. Given `struct fat { int id; int score; char name[60]; };` (declared for you), implement `size_t touched_bytes(const char *layout, size_t n)` — for layout 'interleaved' return n * sizeof(struct fat); for 'split' return n * 2 * sizeof(int) (the hot fields only: id + score, stored in their own array); any other layout (or NULL) returns (size_t)-1. n == 0 returns 0 for any valid layout.

tests.name: interleaved pays for names
tests.hint: Every record drags its 60-byte name through the pass: n times the fat size.

tests.name: split pays hot only
tests.hint: Scores and ids live in their own arrays: 8 bytes per record, names untouched.

tests.name: zero and unknown
tests.hint: Zero records touch nothing; an unknown layout is a caller bug, refused.
